issue.title: test_snapshot_includes_live_config_token_refresh_threads flakes under the full parallel lane
issue.description:
Reported by epic phase `sase-sp.6` as a PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP during the sase-sp landing.
The phase ran a full `just test` on its combined tree (36779 passed, 13 skipped) under
heavy host contention — 27m48s wall clock with many concurrent SASE agent workspaces
live on this machine — and exactly this node failed. An immediate isolated rerun on the
same tree passed.

The subsystem is unrelated to that phase's diff: the phase touched finalizer deferral
adjudication, telemetry, and docs, while this node asserts that the global-state leak
detector's snapshot includes live-config token-refresh threads. That is thread-count
state, which is order- and timing-sensitive under pytest's parallel `-n` lane.

Confirmed still passing in isolation on master at ad9ed74af during the sase-sp landing
turn (1 passed in 2.26s), so the failure is intermittent rather than a standing break.
Serial reproduction has not been attempted; a single full-lane observation is all the
evidence there is.

evidence.note: Independent reproduction on 2026-11-20 during sase-1tz.3.1.5 just check (tool run f01ca08dea2b0fe528cd1660068f0c20, monitor ta55z2xz2qa9). Escalated full scoped lane: 2 failed / 62288 passed / 18 skipped in 1442s. Node tests/test_global_state_leak_detector.py::test_snapshot_includes_live_config_token_refresh_threads failed with AssertionError at tests/_global_state_leak_detector_fingerprints.py:84: _live_config_token_refresh_threads() was nonempty, then capture_process_snapshot() omitted sase.config.core._live_config_token_refresh_threads from snap.globals. Dummy thread hold.wait(timeout=30.0) can expire while the snapshot walk exceeds 30s under load (same run had a leak-snapshot test at 133s). Phase diff is prebuild miss/error split only; locator_paths untouched (triage touched=false). Same full-parallel-lane-only node as this task; already in tests/reproducible_flake_baseline.txt. This run classified NEW because tool-run triage matches flake baseline by failure signature, not node id.
